name: fix-mod-version-notice
about: Issue #24: players with different HammerwatchPlus updates get into one lobby (the game's mod check compares mod ids, not their contents), and only the log said so. Now each package carries its update (tools/build.py), a client in town reports its packages to the host, the host answers with its own, and both are told which packages differ and whose are older; a side that never reports is an update from before these reports. One lab game stands in for two: a host's request runs locally, and `hwp builds fake` reads every report and answer as if the other side ran that.

steps.name: the update is logged in town

steps.pattern: \[HWP\] .+ runs another HammerwatchPlus update than you, so some mods may misbehave together: HWP-qol: yours \d{4}-\d\d-\d\d \([0-9a-f]{7,}\+?\), theirs 2026-10-01 \(0000000\)\. Theirs are older: .+ should update every HammerwatchPlus mod
steps.name: the other side is older: they are told to update

steps.pattern: (?s)updates differ from .+?: HWP-qol: .+?updates differ from .+?: HWP-qol:
steps.name: the host's answer is compared too

steps.pattern: theirs 2099-01-01 \(fffffff\)\. Yours are older: update every HammerwatchPlus mod in the Steam Workshop
steps.name: this side is older: told to update

steps.pattern: \[HWP:core\] no update report from The host in 3 s
steps.name: a host that never answers

steps.pattern: \[HWP:core\] no update report from (?!The host).+ in 3 s
steps.name: a client that never reports

steps.pattern: \[HWP\] The host runs a HammerwatchPlus update from before update checks, older than yours \(\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d \([0-9a-f]{7,}\+?\)\)
steps.name: the older side is named
